content.help: Turns the whole integration layer on or off. Off = nothing is sent to CHIM, nothing is offered to NPCs, nothing is executed.
Emergency stop. Overrides every other setting. A running scene can still be ended with the stop key.

Lines go to the server log (lorerim_glue.log, prefixed GAME). How many is set by How much to log below. Off = nothing is sent to the server at all. Every entry carries a correlation id that also appears in the server log.

Errors only: failures and warnings, nothing else. Normal (the setting for play): the load line, commands, results, snapshot problems, voice and errors - a few lines a minute. Everything (for diagnosis): adds the chatter - conversation holds, ev=facts, initiative ticks, listener re-asserts, calibration summaries, reply timings - and copies every line to the Papyrus log (only written when Papyrus logging is on in Skyrim.ini). A change applies within 30 seconds.

content.text: Tell me when a request fails
content.help: When something an NPC tried could not be done (no bed nearby, someone is watching, the position cannot be reached ...), a short note appears in the corner with the reason. NPCs no longer speak a second line after every action (that made scenes slow), so this note is how you find out.

On every game load the glue writes one corner note with its version and session number. It is the only sign of life that does not go through CHIM, MCM Helper or the server, so if it is missing the scripts are not running at all. Leave it on while anything is being diagnosed.

A tick every 30 seconds that keeps the glue timer alive and renews its CHIM event registrations every two minutes. It costs almost nothing and it is what stops one bad game load leaving the glue silent for the rest of the session. Only turn it off on advice.
When off, NPCs are never offered the action and the game refuses the command. Per-NPC strictness, marriage rules and thresholds live in the server config file (lrg_config.json).
People inside this distance who are awake and can see or hear count as witnesses.
Same, outdoors.

content.text: A closed door makes a room private
content.help: Until now anyone awake and nearby counted as a witness even through a wall or a shut door, so a room in a busy inn could never be private - which is exactly what went wrong. With this on, somebody who cannot see either of you no longer counts just for being close, as long as the door of the room you are in is shut. Anyone who can actually SEE you always counts, door or no door. Off = the old behaviour.

How close somebody has to be to count as a witness when they cannot see you and no door is shut between you. Lower it if scenes are refused in places that feel private, raise it if people walk in on you.

content.text: How near a door counts as this room's door
content.help: Doors within this distance decide whether the room you are standing in is shut. Small rooms need less, a hall needs more. Every door in reach has to be closed for the room to count as private - including the one you came in through.

content.text: Scene control (everything by talking - OStim's own menu is never needed)

content.help: She leads: when you stay passive she moves things along herself, one step at a time, at her own pace. I lead: she only follows what you ask for. You can change it any time by saying so ("you lead", "I'll lead"). Later in a scene you can also tell her to let it run by itself (OStim's auto mode).
How many navigation steps away a requested position may be for a smooth, animated transition (OStim default: 5).

content.text: Jump to positions without a route
content.help: When a requested position has no animated route from the current one, fade out and switch to it directly. This trades a smooth transition for always reaching the position you asked for. Off = such requests are declined.

content.text: Wait before carrying out the second thing you asked for
content.help: When you ask for two things in one breath ("take my clothes off and then lie down"), the second one has to wait until the first is finished. This is how long it may wait before it is given up with a note in the corner - keep it at or above 30, because moving into a new position alone may take 25 seconds. 0 = never wait, which is what the mod did before: the second half was simply lost.

A scene can start on a free bed nearby, and you or she can move it to a bed, chair, table and so on by saying so. OStim's furniture pop-up never appears. Off = scenes always happen standing where you are.

content.text: How far to look for furniture
content.help: Free furniture inside this distance (same floor) counts as in reach.

content.text: Get dressed again after a scene
content.help: When a scene the glue started ends, whatever either of you wore at the start and is still off is put back on, whatever OStim's own redress option says. Weapons and clothes the glue itself removed always come back.

content.text: Switch off OStim's weapon removal (crash fix)
content.help: OStim's own weapon removal crashed the game, both when a scene started and later when it changed position. With this on, the glue switches the three OStim options that reach it off around a scene it starts: 'Remove Weapons at Start' (stays off - it crashes at every start), 'Fully undress mid Scene' and 'Partial Undressing' (both put back exactly as you had them when the scene ends). The glue puts the weapons away itself, gives them back afterwards, and does the mid-scene undressing in OStim's place. Turn this off only if you want OStim to handle weapons and mid-scene undressing itself again (OStim MCM > Undressing).

content.text: Undress you both during a scene
content.help: Only matters while the crash fix above is on. OStim's own mid-scene undressing is paused during a scene the glue started, so the glue takes it over: when a position starts that OStim would have undressed somebody for, the glue undresses them through OStim itself (same clothes, same redress at the end). It follows your OStim setting: with 'Fully undress mid Scene' off in OStim's MCM nothing is undressed here either. Off = clothes stay on until you or she says otherwise ("take it off").

content.text: Refuse to start if hands cannot be emptied
content.help: Crash protection. Before a scene starts the glue puts away weapons, shields, spells and ammunition of both of you (and gives them back afterwards), because OStim crashed the game while doing that itself. If something cannot be put away, the scene is not started. Turn off only for testing.

content.text: Let her finish her line before she moves
content.help: When she starts something herself - a kiss, a new position, undressing, moving to a bed - the game waits until her spoken line has started (and, for the start of a scene, finished) before the animation changes, so nothing ever begins out of nowhere. It waits a few seconds at most and then goes ahead anyway, so nothing is ever lost. Things YOU ask for are never held back. Off = everything happens the moment it is decided, as before.

content.text: Always talk to your partner during a scene
content.help: During a scene there is usually nobody under your crosshair, so what you say can be answered by the Narrator instead of your partner - who then never hears it, and cannot act on it. With this on, your partner stays the one you are talking to for as long as the scene runs, and CHIM's normal routing comes back the moment it ends. This uses a CHIM function whose side effects are not documented: if you ever see her greet you mid-scene, or find yourself still talking to her long after it ended, switch this off - everything else keeps working without it.

content.text: Septims can be part of the arrangement
content.help: Some people can be bought and some cannot, and what it takes depends entirely on who she is - how she lives, what money means to her, whether she wants you anyway. You offer septims, or ask her price, by talking; she names her own figure and haggles in her own words. Septims only ever change hands when SHE agrees; the money is taken when the scene starts, and nothing is given back if you stop early. People who would never sell are never for sale at any price. Off = money is never part of it.

Scales every price. The prices are built from a day's honest wage in Skyrim (about 35 septims), so a tavern girl thinks in a few days of work and a jarl's court in hundreds. Raise it if septims come too easily in your game, lower it if nobody is ever affordable.

content.text: NPCs who make the first move

content.help: An NPC you are dealing with, who is drawn to you, may flirt, invite you somewhere private, or - once you really are alone - make her move, without you asking. Whether and how she does it is up to her character. NPCs who are not interested never do, and cost nothing. Off = NPCs only ever react to what you say.

content.text: How often she gets the chance
content.help: Seconds between two chances, for the NPC you are looking at or talked to a moment ago (within a few steps, nobody talking, no menu open, no fight). The server still lets most chances pass, so this is an upper limit, not a rhythm.

content.text: She stays with you while you are talking
content.help: People you talk to through CHIM used to wander off mid-conversation, back to whatever their schedule said - because nothing in the game was keeping them there. With this on, as soon as either of you says something she stops where she is and turns to face you, and she stays until the conversation is over. She can still talk, gesture and look around; only her feet are held. She is let go the moment the conversation stops, you walk off, a fight starts, a real dialogue menu opens, a scene begins, or you reload. People who must not be held are never held: anyone hostile, guards with business with you, anyone in a scripted scene or on a quest errand, followers, children, and anyone already sitting or asleep.

content.text: Let her go if nobody speaks for
content.help: The conversation counts as over when neither of you has said anything for this long, and then she goes back to her business. Every line from either of you starts the clock again, and she is never cut off in the middle of her own sentence. 0 = switched off, she walks away as before.

content.text: Let her go if you walk this far away
content.help: Walking away ends the conversation, so she is released at this distance - and sooner if you are sneaking off. She is also released the moment you go through a door into another room. Lower it if she follows the conversation further than feels natural.

Leave this off unless you need it. Normally only her feet are held, while whatever her schedule wanted her to do keeps running underneath - with a busy mod-added routine that can show as her turning on the spot or sliding a little. This adds a second layer that suspends the routine itself for as long as the conversation lasts. It works, but it writes something into your save for the length of the hold, so it is the riskier of the two and it is not needed for most people.

Occasional, short lines on meaningful moments only (start, position change, peak). Never looping chatter. The NPC always answers when YOU speak, regardless of this setting. Also needed for her to take the lead.
Chance that a meaningful moment produces a line.
Seconds that must pass between two unprompted lines.

When she leads, and nothing changed and nobody spoke for this long, your partner gets a turn to move things along herself: a new position, a change of pace, clothes - whatever fits her character. She always says a short line for anything she starts herself. Needs the speech toggle above. Raise it if scenes feel like they run away from you, lower it if she waits too long when you stay quiet.

content.text: Leave the lead to me for
content.help: After you ask for something, she takes no turn of her own for this long - she answers you and does what you asked, but she does not move things along on top of it. The server normally names the length itself and this is what the game uses when it does not; whichever is longer wins, so raising it is the way to get more room if she still moves things along while you are steering. Saying "you lead" or "surprise me" ends the hold at once.

How long the game waits for her voice to start before making a change she chose herself - a new position, undressing, moving to a bed. When nothing is heard within this time the change happens anyway. 0 = never wait. Needs 'Let her finish her line before she moves' on the Intimacy page.

content.text: Wait for her line (start of a scene)
content.help: The same for the start of a scene, which waits for her line to FINISH, because OStim's fade would otherwise cut across it. When her voice never arrives the scene starts anyway after this long, so nothing is ever lost - only late. Default 20 s: her voice has to be generated and downloaded first. 0 = never wait.

Her voice arrives sentence by sentence, so the game waits this long after the last one before a scene starts - otherwise the fade can fall into the gap between two sentences. Raise it if a scene still begins while she is talking; lower it if the pause before a scene feels too long.

content.text: Keep her with you afterwards for
content.help: When a scene ends she used to walk off in the same second, often in the middle of her last words. Now she stays with you, facing you, until she has said her goodbye - what the two of you just did, what you are to her now, and where she is going next - and then goes about her business. This is how long her voice has to arrive: while she is actually speaking the wait keeps stretching, so she is never cut off in the middle of her goodbye. If her voice never arrives at all, she is free again after this many seconds. 0 = switched off, she leaves at once as before.

Her voice arrives sentence by sentence, so the game waits this long after the last one before letting her go. Raise it if she turns away in the middle of her goodbye, lower it if she stands around after she has clearly finished.

content.text: Only after a scene of at least
content.help: A scene that was over almost before it began gets no goodbye - she simply carries on. Raise it if you get a goodbye after something that barely happened. The goodbye and the small relationship gain have separate thresholds (the gain needs a full minute), so a very short scene can give you one without the other.

content.text: Let her go if you walk this far away
content.help: If you walk off, go through a door or a fight starts, she is released immediately - she is never left standing. This is the distance at which that happens.

content.text: Keep talking to her after a scene for
content.help: When a scene ends, what you say next is meant for her - but at that exact moment the game has nobody under your crosshair, so CHIM can answer as the Narrator instead and she never hears you. With this on she stays the one you are talking to for this long after the scene, and for as long as the conversation keeps going; then normal routing comes back. She is also let go at once if you walk away, turn to somebody else, a fight starts, or a new scene begins. 0 = off.
Once she has finished her goodbye and you have said nothing more, this is how long the game waits before handing the conversation back to whoever you are looking at.

content.text: Give me my camera back after a scene
content.help: If a scene ever leaves you in OStim's free camera, or without movement or look controls, the game puts them back a moment after it ends. It only ever does this when they really are still gone - never during a quest scene, a menu or another scene - and it writes a line in the log every time it fires.

How plain the language is whenever things are romantic or sexual with an interested adult NPC - flirting, invitations, before, during and after a scene. Suggestive: hints only. Direct: says it plainly. Explicit: nothing held back, crude words included. The character's personality and the setting still shape how she talks. Ordinary conversations, and NPCs who are not interested, are never affected.

content.text: Do not freeze while undressed for a scene
content.help: While a scene runs, or while the glue has taken your clothes off, the cold you would build up is given back through Survival Mode Improved's own interface. Only does anything if that mod is installed. NPCs do not feel cold in that mod, so this is about you only.
Raise it if you still get colder during a scene in a freezing place, lower it if scenes warm you up more than a fire would. 0 = nothing.

Ends a running scene immediately. Default: End. Saying "let's stop" works too, but this is the guaranteed route - it is the one that still works when the glue has gone quiet (an unconfirmed adult, a child nearby, the feature switched off).

Menuless questing module: writes the topics the glue sees for the crosshair NPC, to compare against the vanilla menu, and writes the diagnostics counters and the self-test to the log in the same press. If no conversation is open it opens a normal visible one with the NPC you are looking at.

Set it to the key you hold to talk to CHIM (default Left Ctrl, the key CHIM uses on this install). It only tells her you are about to speak, so she waits instead of carrying on by herself when there is only one thing to say (see 'Let her carry on by herself' on the Menuless questing page). If you change CHIM's key, change this one too; clear it and she simply carries on after the short breath and answers your words on the next line.

content.text: The leave-the-conversation key of the menuless questing module is on the Menuless questing page.

content.help: On (the default): when you talk business with somebody, her real list of things to say comes up on screen - the same list you would get by pressing E - and stays there. You never have to click it: say what you want in your own words and the glue picks the matching line for you; her real reply plays and the game runs its own effects, exactly as if you had clicked. You can still click any line yourself at any moment, and nothing ever takes the list away. It learns what it needs from your first conversation with anyone (even one you open with E). The first line it ever picks for you must be a simple one - a question, a bit of small talk - and until one has been picked, a line that would move a quest along is left for you to click, and she tells you so. Off: nothing is ever clicked and the glue never opens a conversation itself; it still reads the list and tells the NPC what business is on the table. While a list is on screen, hotkeys of other mods that go quiet in dialogue stay quiet (OStim's and OBody's keys, Hot Key Skill, Simplest Horses, Thieving XP and this mod's own NPC initiative) - that is normal and ends with the conversation. Trade is NOT behind this switch: asking a merchant what she has for sale opens her real barter window (real prices) right after her line, whatever this switch and the dry run say. This switch is for quest lines, rooms, rides and training through her real dialogue.

content.text: Menuless questing: dry run (nothing is clicked)
content.help: Everything runs - the list is read and the NPC decides which line she would pick - but nothing is clicked: the log says WOULD CLICK, the list stays on screen for you to click yourself, and she tells you the menuless dry run is on. It ships OFF and never switches itself on or off: tick it only to watch what it would pick without it picking. This is NOT the developer dry run: that one is 'DEV: dry-run everything' at the bottom of the Diagnostics page, it stops EVERYTHING NPCs do (undressing, scenes, follow / wait / release, services), and it should stay OFF for play.

content.text: Send quest talk to the server
content.help: On (the default) is what this version expects. Turn it OFF only if you have rolled the server side back to the previous version: an older server does not know these messages and would answer each of them as an ordinary paid reply, reading the raw data aloud as if you had said it. Off means the game sends nothing about conversations at all - no topic lists, no subtitles, no results - so the whole feature is inert and costs nothing, and everything else (intimacy, snapshots, initiative) keeps working. The two halves of this version are meant to be installed together, server first.

content.text: Let her carry on by herself when there is only one thing to say
content.help: On (the default): when the next line is the only thing to say and changes nothing by itself (the oath lines, 'The Greybeards?'), it plays by itself a short breath (2.5 seconds) after the line before it has gone from the screen - or, if you asked her something in that breath, a short breath after her answer ends - unless you press your talk key (Keys page) in that breath; then it waits for your words. A line with a cost, a quest step of its own or a goodbye always waits for your words. Needs dialogue subtitles on; with them off, every such line waits for your voice. Off: every line waits for your words.

content.text: What the glue may take over
Guards, arrests and bounties: always yours to click
content.help: There is no switch for this, on purpose: an arrest, a fine or a jail term is the one thing that cannot be undone by talking. While a guard who has something against you is talking to you - you have a bounty in her hold, or an arrest line is on her list - her list stays on screen and nothing on it is ever picked for you, at any setting: you click it yourself (for example 'I submit. Take me to jail.'), and if you ask her for a line on it she tells you to choose it yourself. Resisting arrest is never picked for you either. A guard with nothing against you is an ordinary conversation. (The two settings that used to sit here and on the Services and truth page could never change this, so they are gone.)

Whether the glue may OPEN a conversation with somebody who is inside a scene. With 'Unless a journal quest owns it' (the default) she may be spoken to at a map table, during a performance or in tavern patter; a scene whose quest has an unfinished objective in your journal is never interrupted. 'Never' leaves everybody inside any scene alone. A conversation you or the game open inside such a scene still shows her list; until the first line has been picked for you, she tells you to choose on it yourself. CHIM's own 'restrict on scene' setting does NOT cover what YOU say, which is why this exists.

options: Unless a journal quest owns it

content.text: May open a conversation to find out
content.help: When your words name some business and no conversation with her is open, the glue can open one so her real list is on screen: a service you ask for (a room, a ride, her wares), joining her faction, words close to a line of hers it has seen before, a real opening line of this load order, or words close to one of her own lines in a quest in your journal. Merely being part of a quest is not enough. She says a word first and her list comes up a few seconds later; it costs no extra AI reply. Opening costs a greeting line (and, rarely, a one-time greeting is spent). Off = the NPC answers in her own words until a conversation happens for another reason.

content.text: Stay out of scripted intro scenes (Helgen)
content.help: On (the default): while the game runs a scripted intro you are inside - Helgen's Unbound from the cart onward on this load order - the glue stands aside: no snapshots, nobody is held or followed, no follow-me, no quest entry, no NPC initiative, no conversation is opened for you and nothing on a dialogue list is picked for you (a list the game shows is yours to click), and CHIM's own move / follow actions are withheld from that scene's actors, so nothing of the glue's can stall the script. NPCs still answer in words, and anything they cannot take up is refused with the reason said aloud. One line in the log when it engages and one when it releases (search for QUIET). The quests it applies to are a short built-in list (MQ101 from stage 5). Off: the glue behaves as before inside such scenes.

content.text: How long it waits for the server
content.help: How long the glue waits for the NPC's decision about a list it just read. When nothing comes, nothing is picked and the list simply stays on screen for you - the conversation is never closed.

content.text: Quiet time before the first click
content.help: Before the first line of a conversation is picked for you, the glue waits until her greeting has stayed on screen unchanged for this long; every later pick waits until her voice has stopped. Raise it if a greeting is ever cut off, lower it if the first exchange feels slow.

content.text: How close she has to be
content.help: The glue refuses to start a conversation from further away than this, and the game's own dialogue distance still wins when it is smaller.

content.text: Reading the list (leave these on automatic)

content.help: 0 = work it out automatically (leave it here). 3 and 4 force one of the two ways of reading the list. 0 also means 'use what the glue measured for itself' - see the Calibration page. The third way (5) reads screen rows instead of list positions and can therefore never be used to click, which is why it cannot be set here at all.

0 = work it out automatically. 0 also means 'use what the glue measured for itself' - see the Calibration page. 1, 2 and 3 force one of the three ways of counting the list; the log's CALIB SUMMARY line (cm=) says which one it measured. If none of them ever works, the feature stops there rather than guessing.

How many topics are read with everything the NPC needs to judge them. The rest are still counted and their texts still sent, so nothing is ever invisible to her - a job at position nineteen is still on the table. 0 = as many as your machine can afford, measured while you play. Anything else is your own number and wins.
The upper limit for the texts-only pass over a very long list (an innkeeper with a job board, a follower with a command menu). 0 = do not read past the number above.

Automatic starts from which dialogue interface mod wins on your install and proves it with the first real click it makes (the Calibration page then says 'route proven'). If a click does not take twice, or on route A nothing answers it within 9 seconds, the next attempt uses the other route. One click per decision, always. A and B force one route.

content.text: Persuade, threaten, bribe and lie in ordinary talk

content.help: When you try to talk somebody round, frighten them, buy them off or lie to them in an ordinary conversation, the outcome is decided by the game's own rules - your Speech skill, your perks, the amulet, your level against theirs - and not by the NPC's imagination. A success gives Speech experience the way the game gives it; a failure is remembered, so the same trick does not work twice. Off = the NPC just answers in character. Every attempt is written to lorerim_glue.log as a line beginning 'check npc=' with the kind, the difficulty, the numbers that went in and the result - if nothing appears there, your words were not recognised as an attempt at all.
Shifts how hard those attempts are. Below zero is kinder, above zero is harsher. What is at stake and how the NPC feels about you still matter more than this.

Off by default on purpose: Beneficial Speech Checks pays out a reward on the persuade/bribe/intimidate counters, and an attempt you made in ordinary conversation is not a quest speech check. Turn it on if you would rather have them counted.

content.text: A failed threat can turn ugly
content.help: Off by default: this is the one consequence that can get you killed over a mis-heard word. On, somebody who was already hostile to you may attack after a threat that failed.

content.text: NPCs know the business between you
content.help: An NPC who is part of a quest you are actually running may refer to what is still unfinished between the two of you, in her own words. Only quests she is part of, only the objective you have already been shown, never a later step - nothing is ever spoiled.

content.text: How much of it at once
content.help: The most unfinished matters an NPC is reminded of in one turn.

content.text: Tell me when she has something
content.help: A short note in the corner when the conversation the glue just read really does contain something quest-related, so you know there is something worth asking about.

content.text: She can say what you can ask her
content.help: 'What can I ask you?' / 'Anything I should know?' - she answers in character from what the glue has actually seen of her list. If it has never seen one, she is vaguer on purpose and says so in her own way.

content.text: She can tell you where you left off
content.help: 'What should I do next?' / 'Where was I?' - answered from your own journal, current objective only, never a later step, never a stage number. The Narrator answers it when nobody is in front of you.

Ends the business politely: the glue takes the NPC's own way out (a 'never mind' topic when the conversation offers one), otherwise it closes the conversation the way the menu's own exit button does. While a guard who has something against you is talking to you it closes nothing - the list stays yours to click. If you rebind CHIM's push-to-talk, set 'Your talk key (CHIM's push-to-talk)' on the Keys page to the same key. Keep this key and your talk key off E, Tab, Enter, Space, W A S D, the arrow keys and every mouse button, because the dialogue menu itself uses those.

content.text: Advanced - leave alone unless the log tells you otherwise

content.help: CHIM blanks an NPC's voice for about a minute after it speaks for her, and the glue puts the real voice back before it opens anything. With this on it goes ahead even when it could not - useful for testing, but the NPC's real lines play silently.

Opens a conversation without the activation extras other mods add. Only switch this on if opening a conversation often needs a second try - the log then says so (search it for 'needed more than one try').

What the glue has learned about the dialogue menu on your install. '4 of 4 learned' means the four things it reads from any dialogue menu are known; 'route proven by N clicks' means a line it picked for you really went through. 'learning: N of 4 - talk to anyone once' means it has not seen enough yet - open any conversation once, even with E. When 'learning' gives another reason instead (the list cannot be counted or read, or the dialogue interface is not one it knows), one more conversation will not fix it by itself and nothing is picked for you until it is; the log says more. 'blocked' names a Smart Talk setting that must be 0 in Data/SKSE/Plugins/SmartTalk.ini (bSkipImmediateOnInput, bHoldToSkip, bSkipOnInteraction); leave Smart Talk's iPapyrusHandle at 3. The same picture is written to lorerim_glue.log on every load and whenever you press the topic-dump key - search it for CALIB SUMMARY.

Starts the measuring again from nothing: the four things it learned, the click route it proved, and the install file it keeps (Data/SKSE/Plugins/LoreRimGlue_calibration.ini), so a save you load afterwards does not get them back from that file. A save made before you pressed this still remembers what it had learned, and playing it writes that back. The server is told too, so the first line picked for you afterwards must be a simple one again. Talk to anyone once and it learns again (the corner note says when).

content.text: Handle rooms, rides, training and trade by talking
content.help: When she really has the dialogue for it, asking out loud - 'a room for the night', 'take me to Morthal', 'can you train me in Alchemy' - uses her REAL entry, with the real price and the real rules of this modlist, instead of CHIM's built-in shortcut. Trade: 'what have you got for sale' / 'let me see your wares' opens her real barter window (real prices) right after her line - no menuless questing needed. Rooms, rides and training use her real entry while 'Quest talk without the menu' is on; with it off, CHIM's own Rent Room / Hire Carriage / Training answer those requests. Until one simple line has been picked for you, she asks you for a simple question first, and she says so whenever she cannot do something.

content.text: Fall back to CHIM's own shortcuts
content.help: When no conversation can be read at all, CHIM's own Rent Room / Hire Carriage / Training actions stay available as a rough stand-in. Switch off if you would rather she simply said she cannot help. This never affects trade: a merchant's barter window is the real one, with the real prices.
'Take me to the Solitude Lighthouse' picks that exact place off her list. If two places could be meant, she asks instead of guessing.

content.text: She may say prices out loud
content.help: Only ever a price her list actually showed. She will never invent one.

content.text: What she is allowed to claim
Only let her state what the game confirmed
content.help: Prices, fares, your bounty, your septims, the outcome of a persuasion and your current task are handed to her as facts. Anything else she is told to be honest about not knowing, rather than making up a number.

content.text: Do not let a wrong number cost me septims
content.help: If she names a price the game has not confirmed AND the same reply tries to act on it, the action is dropped - she said something wrong out loud, which happens, but nothing was spent.

content.text: She knows who travels with you
content.help: Tells the AI, in words, that this person is your companion, which framework she belongs to, whether she is following or waiting, and how many companion slots you have left. Also makes the glue count your own companions separately from strangers, so 'my companion is right there' no longer reads as 'a stranger is watching'. Off = nothing about followers is sent at all.

content.text: Follower commands use her real dialogue
content.help: 'Come with me', 'wait here', 'follow me', 'you're dismissed', 'let's trade', 'this is your home now' go through the follower framework's OWN dialogue entry when she has one - so the real rules apply (Requiem's recruitment conditions, the slot limit, her own dismissal lines) and CHIM's rough shortcuts step aside for that turn instead of firing as well.

content.text: Never hold someone who is already walking with you
content.help: The conversation hold stops people wandering off mid-sentence. It always left real followers alone; this also leaves alone the two kinds of companion the teammate flag does not show - one CHIM told to follow you, and one CHIM half-recruited - because holding her while a follow order runs underneath is what makes her fidget on the spot.

content.text: 'Follow me' can pull her out of a performance
content.help: A bard on her stage or someone busy with an idle routine is held by that scene, and no follow order can move her until it ends. With this on, when you ask her to come with you the glue ends that one scene the way the game's own 'stop playing' line does and lets her follow. Never a scene of a quest in your journal, a main or faction quest or a courier. Off = she stays in her scene and says so.

content.text: She follows you like a real follower
content.help: CHIM's own 'follow me' keeps her about four times farther away than the game's own followers (512 / 1024 units against their 128 / 256) and only follows while she can see you - so indoors she stands still, then runs to catch up, then stops well short of you. With this on the glue lays its own follow package over CHIM's, with the game's follower distances and no line-of-sight rule: she walks when you walk and runs only when you run. Also covers a follow CHIM started by itself. Off = CHIM's follow exactly as it is.

content.text: 'Follow me' hands her to Simple Follower Framework
content.help: Asked to come along, she becomes your real companion through Simple Follower Framework - the same recruit its own 'Follow me, I need your help' line makes - so its own follow package, 'wait here' and 'you can go' (she waits; parting ways for good stays her own dialogue) apply, and every follower mod sees her: the follower marker, trade, Swiftly Order Squad, doors and cell changes. She then walks at the game's own follower distance (farther than the natural follow above, not closer), and with the framework's Follower Sandbox on she wanders inside inns and homes. Needs a free companion slot (one per 25 Speech) and someone the game lets you recruit; otherwise she walks with you the old way and says why. A companion CHIM tries to move itself is handed back to her framework. Off = the old way always.

content.text: CHIM's own 'join my party' was written for a follower mod this modlist does not use. Here it puts the person in the game's follower faction and stops - no companion slot, no framework, no way to dismiss her. Worse, the game's dismiss line then goes to whoever your real follower is. Switch 'Join my party' off in the CHIM web interface (Actions), and leave the repair below on.

content.help: Checked when you talk to her, and once after every load. Nothing happens to anybody who was recruited properly.

Make her real: if you have a companion slot free she becomes a proper follower of the framework, so wait / follow / trade / dismiss all work on her. Undo it: she is taken back out of the follower faction and simply walks with you the way CHIM makes people walk with you. Only tell me: nothing is changed, the log says what was found.

options: Make her real if there is room

content.text: How long she takes to answer
Time how long she takes to answer
content.help: Writes one line per reply: how long you waited for the words, and how long again before her voice started. Costs nothing and sends nothing to the AI. Search lorerim_glue.log for lines beginning LAT. Every reply is logged only when General - How much to log is Everything; a reply slower than the limit below is logged at Normal too.

content.text: Warn me when a reply takes longer than
content.help: Milliseconds. A note in the corner, so a slow model or a stalled voice is visible rather than mysterious.

content.text: Most of that wait is the language model, not the glue: on this install a spoken turn is about 7.7 seconds in total, of which the model is about 6.5 and everything the server does is about 0.6. The voice number is the part nothing else has ever measured.
Developer switch - leave this OFF for play
DEV: dry-run everything (nothing NPCs do will happen)
content.help: A developer switch. With it ON every command an NPC tries is refused and only written to the log as WOULD: undressing, starting or changing a scene, follow / wait / release, dialogue clicks, rooms, rides and training - nothing at all happens, whatever you say. It ships OFF. While it is on, NPCs will SAY that the LoreRim Glue dry-run switch is on, a message box says so on every game load and a corner note repeats it every two minutes, so it can never be on by accident without you knowing. This is NOT the menuless-questing dry run - that one is 'Menuless questing: dry run (nothing is clicked)' on the Menuless questing page, it only concerns quest talk, and it ships off as well. Saying "stop" still ends a running scene with this on.
